newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Goldfields cannot explain share fall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Goldfields cannot explain share fall.

text.p: Gold miner Goldfields Ltd said on Wednesday it was unaware of any non-compliance with the disclosure rules of the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) and could not explain the recent fall in its share price.

The company said several factors could have affected the value of its shares, including the release of its 995/96 profit statement on August 28 and the announcement of a forecast net profit for 1996/97 between A$20 million to A$25 million.
It said this was below the profit forecast of AS30 million to A$46 million included in the Part A statement for its takeover of Pancontinental Mining Ltd.
Goldfields reported a full year net profit of A$14.19 million for the year to June 30, 1996.
The company also cited market comment regarding the possible sale by the Papua New Guinean government of its interest in local mining operations, including the giant Porgera gold mine.
Goldfields, which has a 25 percent stake in Porgera, is about 57 percent owned by RGC Ltd.
Goldfields shares last traded at A$2.35 on Tuesday.
The ASX had asked the company if it could explain the fall in its share price from A$2.84 on September 2.
